note: Research/design constraints are not CC-PRIN-* principles and not settled doctrine. They bind architecture and research so the framework does not invent franchise gatekeeping while exploring civic education or youth participation.

constraints.title: No Knowledge Qualification for Suffrage
constraints.text: Constitutional Capitalism may advocate universal civic preparation and may investigate age-16 local suffrage, but civic education, testing, certification, academic achievement, service hours, or political knowledge shall not be prerequisites for exercising the franchise.
constraints.philosophical_line: Educate everyone; enfranchise by law — not by examination.

sequencing_rule.first: Build strong universal civic education and participation infrastructure (government, constitutional structure, local institutions, economics, media literacy, evidence evaluation, deliberation, voting mechanics, community service, practical participation).
sequencing_rule.then: Separately study extending local voting rights to age 16 as a democratic reform hypothesis — not as a reward for completing a civics program.

constraints.rejected_framing: Complete our civics program and earn the right to vote at 16.
constraints.correct_framing: Society has an obligation to prepare every young person for citizenship. Separately, the framework proposes examining whether citizens should begin exercising local suffrage at 16.
constraints.unintended_consequence_blocked: If civic training became a voting qualification, whoever controlled curriculum, tests, certification, exemptions, or funding could indirectly control access to the franchise — conflicting with Constitutional Symmetry.
